evals.prompt: I'm the only grants person at Valley Roots Farmworker Health, a 501(c)(3) in Yakima County, Washington (budget about $2.3M, founded 2011). We need to fund a new mobile clinic program, roughly $180K/year starting July 2027, and we'd like 3-4 grants of $25K-$75K each. Can you lay out how to find and vet foundation and government prospects, and give me a fit-scoring rubric and prospect list format I can use? We currently have renewals with two local funders and don't know when they're eligible again.
evals.expected_output: A search brief and source plan (Candid/FDO, 990-PFs, grants.gov and the state portal, peer funders), plus a weighted fit rubric that screens geography first with a minimum threshold and a prospect-list format. It also covers a 12-18 month grant calendar and a renewal tracker, notes the heavier compliance of government grants, and ends with a hand-off to grant writing.
assertions: Starts with a search brief (program area, ask range, geography, eligibility constraints) and names sources including Candid/Foundation Directory, 990-PF filings, grants.gov or the state grants portal, and peer organizations' listed funders

Provides a fit rubric covering mission alignment, geographic eligibility, grant size fit, applicant eligibility, cycle timing and relationship strength, scored with a minimum threshold, and says to check geography first
Tells the user to verify stated priorities and typical grant size against the funder's actual 990-PF grant history, not website language
Includes a rolling 12-18 month grant calendar (LOI, proposal, decision and report dates) and a renewal tracker, and advises reviewing the two existing renewals before cold prospecting
Notes that government grants carry heavier compliance (e.g., 2 CFR 200 Uniform Guidance, indirect rate rules) and says to confirm current rules at the source
Ends at the 'apply to this funder by this date' point and hands off drafting to nonprofit-grant-writing with a funder profile brief

evals.prompt: is the Hollis Family Foundation worth applying to? their site says they fund 'youth development nationally.' we're a $400k after-school robotics program in Dayton OH and want $50k. how do I tell quickly if it's a good fit
evals.expected_output: A quick fit check: pull the 990-PF to see actual grants (size, geography, recipients), run the scoring rubric, and decide against a threshold, with specific warnings about website language and median grant size.
assertions: Recommends pulling the foundation's 990-PF (e.g., via ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer or Candid) to see actual grants made, recipient geography and typical grant size
Warns that 'youth development nationally' website language may not match actual giving, which is often narrower in practice
Compares the foundation's median or typical grant to the $50K ask and suggests a smaller first request if the median is much lower
Applies the fit rubric (mission, geography, size, eligibility, timing, relationship) with a go/no-go threshold, and checks for invitation-only or LOI-gated processes
Asks about or credits any board or staff connection to a trustee or program officer as raising win probability

evals.prompt: Our ED at Hilltop Senior Center wants me to go after the Gates Foundation and the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation this year because 'big names = big money.' I've also got 3 proposals all due the week of March 9 and I'm one person. We're a $750K org serving one rural county in Kentucky. Help me make the case for a better plan.
evals.expected_output: The response pushes back on chasing prestige over fit, using the rubric's geography and size gates and pointing to renewals or strong-fit regional funders first. It flags the clustered March 9 deadlines as a capacity conflict to escalate and sequence, and suggests a writing-capacity plan.
assertions: Names 'chasing prestige over fit' as a failure mode and recommends scoring the big foundations on the fit rubric (geography, size fit, eligibility, invitation-only processes) before investing time
Recommends reviewing renewals and lapsed good-fit funders and lower-profile regional or community funders before cold prospecting national names
Flags three proposals in the same week as a capacity conflict to escalate to the development lead or ED to sequence or reassign drafting
Recommends a shared grant calendar and a writing-capacity plan (how many LOIs or proposals per month staff time supports)
Does not assert specific current priorities or eligibility rules for Gates or RWJF as fact; frames them as things to verify

should_not_trigger.query: Write a two-page letter of inquiry to the Meyer Memorial Trust for our housing navigation program.
A local bank wants to be the presenting sponsor of our fun run in exchange for logo placement — how should we price that?
